Now the news in detail Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said India's progress draws strength
from its rich cultural heritage, scientific achievements and modern infrastructure.
The Prime Minister was speaking after inaugurating and laying foundation stones of development
projects worth over 13,000 crore rupees across Tamil Nadu at an event held at IHM
address today. The projects span road and rail transport, port infrastructure, petroleum and
scientific research.
This is a historic day for Tamil Nadu. Today's program involves projects worth 13,000 crore
rupees. We are inaugurating many completed projects and laying foundations for new ones.
Some will make daily travel easier. Others will spend them, industry and trade together.

I congratulate the people of the state on this occasion."
Recalling his interactions with former Tamil Nadu chief ministers, the prime minister said
that despite changes in governments, his commitment to the development of Tamil Nadu and the
welfare of its people had remained unchanged.
The prime minister cited Tamil Nadu's temples, scientific institutions and metro rail
network as examples of how tradition and modern development can go hand in hand. The Prime
Minister also extended Navaratri greetings to the people of the state. Earlier in the
day, Mr. Mubudi inaugurated the Poonamalli Vada Palani stretch of phase 2 of the Chennai
metro rail project built at a cost of around 4900 crore rupees. The Prime Minister and
Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay jointly flagged off the new metro services and travelled
on the train. Prime Minister Narendra Modi also attended

The Supreme Court today directed authorities to ensure that people gathering peacefully
are not illegally detained and that the free movement of people is a loud subject to traffic
regulations.
It also called for review of barricading arrangements in Delhi and directed the center to ensure
that metro services operate according to their normal schedule and that internet services
remain uninterrupted subject to law and order requirements.
The court also said metro and train services should function normally in accordance with
the prevailing law and order situation.
It further directed that lawyers must not be obstructed from discharging their professional
duties, issuing notice to the center on a plea, seeking initiation of contempt proceedings
against authorities over alleged violations of its directions.
The Supreme Court said it would hear all parties and ensure that no inconvenience was caused.
The Delhi Police today said that upon receiving information about the death of the grandmother
of CJP founder Abhijit Deepke, officers approached him to convey the news and offered all possible
assistance.
DCP Neha Yadav said this while briefing the media in New Delhi this afternoon.
As soon as Delhi Police received information about the death of Abhijit Deepke's grandmother,
other, police personnel approached him to convey the sad news. They offered him all possible
assistance, including arranging flights, facilitating phone calls or meeting any other needs. He
was repeatedly asked whether he wished to speak to his parents, but he declined. After
giving him some time to process the news, the officers asked again whether he needed
any assistance. These facts have been misrepresented in the CJP's press conference.
India today called out the office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights, OHCHR, for its
double standards and approach of extreme selectivity when it comes to public positions while rejecting
the organization's remarks on yesterday's events in New Delhi.
In a statement, External Affairs Minister Spokesperson Randhir Jayaswal described the OHCHR's remarks
as unwarranted and unacceptable.
The OHCHR has an approach of extreme selectivity when it comes to public positions.
Violent responses to protests in our neighbourhood have gone uncommented,
as indeed have law enforcement actions in its own vicinity.
Such double standards only erode the credibility of its standing
and contribute to the loss of faith in multilateralism.
This spokesperson highlighted that India is the world's largest democracy
where the right to peaceful assembly is guaranteed by the constitution and safeguarded by robust
institutions.
India is the world's largest democracy where the right to peaceful assembly is guaranteed
by a constitution and safeguarded by robust institutions and independent judiciary and
a free media.
As in every democracy, Indian citizens exercise this right subject to the maintenance of
public order and safety.
A law enforcement authorities act strictly in accordance with the law and our courts

Welcome back to the news at 9.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined
by the mantra of Janaseva Siddesh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues.
Guided by this vision for Seva and Susarshan, the government has been ceaselessly working
towards achieving the goal of a vixit Bharat by 2047.
Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming
lives today.
In a special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated
initiated into action through initiatives aimed at removing the colonial mindset.
The history of modern India is deeply entangled with two centuries of British colonialism and
decades after independence.
Over the past few years, the government has slowly been steering India away from these
vestiges of British rule, addressing the nation from the Red Fort on the 76th Independence
Day in 2022, the Prime Minister Narendra Modi, outlined five resolutions or punch
Pran for the next 25 years.
Elaborating on the second Pran, he said, in no part of citizens' existence, not even
in the deepest corners of mind or habits, should there be any ounce of slavery.
In a concerted effort to free the country from its colonial legacy and promote a distinct
Indian's identity, the government has undertaken a series of initiatives across various sectors.
The historic Rajpat in New Delhi was renamed Kartavipat and inaugurated by the Prime
Minister in 2022.
Similarly, a grand statue of freedom fighter Netaji Subhashchand Bose was installed near
India Gate which has replaced the statue of King George V. BJP leader Ramadav has said
that restoring India's cultural and civilizational identity is a symbol of self-respect. He added
that decolonization is the real patriotism that is happening today.
We lived as a nation for not less than 5,000 years. In that long history we created
a great nation, great history, great monuments, great historical places that has been India's
more than 1,500 obsolete laws have been repealed in recent years as part of efforts to simplify
governance and remove outdated legal provisions.
These initiatives reflect the government's stated commitment to building a confident,
self-reliant India rooted in its cultural heritage and national values.
Akshit Vardyanakashwani, Delhi.
Nepal has been hit by flash floods once again, as the Booty Gandhaki River swept Gorkha district
in the VRs today, washing away settlements in Chamnobri rural municipality.
Nepalese authorities have rescued more than 80 people so far, including 9 foreign nationals.
Five people still remain missing.
The flood swept away houses and bridges and damaged several hydropower projects.
The International Center for Integrated Mountain Development has suggested that the
flash flood may have been triggered by the sudden failure of a temporary blockage form
by a landslide near Chumche in Gorkha district. Floodwaters carrying mud, sediments and debris
surged downstream, prompting authorities to issue warnings for communities along the
Bouddhi Gandaki Trishuli and Narayani river systems.
Pakistan has declared an emergency in Khaybar Pakhtunkhwa province, amid a deteriorating
low on order situation in the northwestern region, effectively bringing the provincial
government to an end. According to the presidential proclamation, President Asif Ali Zardari
invoked emergency provision citing a breakdown of constitutional machinery in the province.
The move allows Pakistan's federal government to assume key executive and legislative powers.
The development comes amid an ongoing protest,
March led by Khaybar Pakhtunkhu, Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, who is demanding the release
of former Prime Minister Imran Khan and access to medical treatment for him.
The nine-day festival of Shraddhi and Navaratri began with religious fervour and devotion across the country today.
People worship Goddess Durga in her nine forms during the festival.
Thousands of devotees throng temples to offer prayers and seek blessings,
as special rituals, traditional ceremonies and devotional celebrations mark the auspicious occasion.
In Gujarat, thousands of devotees visited the 400-year-old Juna Ambaji temple at Gopipura in Surat
to attend the morning Mangala Arati and offer prayers to Goddess Amba.
Straightwise celebrations kicked off with Ghatasthapana
and the lighting of traditional Garbo lamps were more from our correspondent.
The festival of Navratri, which literally means nine nights,
is one of the biggest dance festivals in the world.
In Gujarat, Navratri is celebrated by playing the traditional folk dance Garba in groups,
observing fasts and performing Arati of Goddess Amba in communities,
Adorned with vibrant lighting, cities across the state have taken on a festive look as
streets reverberate with traditional garba music.
The Gujarat police has made elaborate security arrangements across more than 22,000 garba
venues.
Special she-teams and police personnel are deployed at party plots and street garba grounds.
The cyber cell is monitoring social media 24-7 to prevent rumours.
